html:
The Otoe, who call themselves Jiwere, are a Siouan people of the central Plains. The map shows them along the Missouri River in what is now southeast Nebraska and northwest Missouri. Their Chiwere language is shared with the Iowa and the Missouria, and is related to that of the Ho-Chunk.

Oral tradition says the three peoples once lived with the Ho-Chunk near the Great Lakes and moved southwest. The Otoe lived in earth lodge villages, farmed maize, beans and squash, and hunted bison on the plains. Their neighbours were the Omaha and the Pawnee.

In 1804 the Lewis and Clark Expedition held its first council with Native leaders, meeting Otoe and Missouria chiefs at a place they named Council Bluff. Later treaties took their land, and in 1881 the joined Otoe-Missouria moved to Indian Territory, now Oklahoma. See also Oto.
